Job Description:

AI Engineering Intern
Role Overview
The AI Engineering Intern (Intern) supports the design, development, testing, and deployment of artificial intelligence solutions across the organization. This hands-on role provides exposure to core AI engineering practices—including model development, data preparation, and prototype creation—while contributing to supervised project tasks. Working closely with senior engineers, the intern builds foundational skills in coding standards, version control, evaluation techniques, and cloud-native development workflows. The intern collaborates with cross-functional teams, applies academic concepts to enterprise-scale systems, and gains the experience needed to grow into an entry-level engineering role.

This role emphasizes learning and skill development while delivering on assigned components, working under close supervision with frequent check-ins and code reviews, and building foundational technical skills and understanding of engineering practices. Successful interns demonstrate curiosity, initiative, and responsiveness to feedback.

In this role, you will:

- Support the development of AI models and prototypes through data preparation, scripting, and experimentation

- Assist in implementing components of AI pipelines, including preprocessing, model training, and testing workflows

- Participate in code reviews and supervised engineering tasks to learn best practices

- Contribute to documentation of prototypes, experiments, and engineering processes

- Execute test cases and validation procedures to verify model performance and reliability

- Analyze datasets to extract insights and generate features under guidance

- Learn cloud-based tools, containerization, and orchestration concepts relevant to AI deployment

- Collaborate with team members to solve technical problems and complete scoped tasks

- Follow established coding, security, and compliance guidelines

- Explore emerging AI technologies and frameworks to build foundational understanding

Qualifications

- Pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field

- Working knowledge of foundational programming concepts and data structures, with exposure to Python

- Familiarity with core AI/ML concepts gained through coursework or independent projects

- Ability to communicate technical ideas clearly and collaborate effectively within a team

- Exposure to cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, along with containerization concepts including Docker and Kubernetes

- Introductory understanding of CI/CD practices and distributed computing fundamentals

- Curiosity-driven approach to learning, with responsiveness to feedback and coaching

- Some grounding in generative AI frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Hugging Face

- Beginning awareness of LLM concepts, including RAG workflows, vector databases, and fine-tuning techniques

Preferred Qualifications

- Academic or project-based experience applying AI/ML concepts

- Awareness of low-code automation platforms such as Microsoft Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate)

- Familiarity with developer-focused AI tools such as Replit Agent or similar agentic coding platforms

Minimum Knowledge Expectations
All candidates for Crowe Studio positions are expected to demonstrate baseline AI and technical knowledge, regardless of role or level.

Core Knowledge Areas
All Crowe Studio team members are expected to have working knowledge in the following areas:

- Basic ML/AI literacy (training vs inference, knowledge cutoffs, LLM fundamentals)

- Prompt engineering and instruction hierarchies

- Context window and context management

- Model selection and capabilities

- Fine-tuning vs prompting vs RAG

- Hallucination and grounding strategies

- Guardrails and output validation

- Evals and testing approaches

- Security and PII awareness

- Responsible AI and governance

- LLM APIs and integration standards

- RAG and vector search

- Vector databases and embeddings

- Agentic workflows and tool use

- Cost and performance awareness

- Common enterprise use cases

What We Look For
Beyond technical knowledge, we look for candidates who demonstrate:

- Intellectual curiosity – asking thoughtful questions and seeking deeper understanding

Topic Content: The rapid advancement of AI Agents is set to have a far-reaching and transformative impact on daily life. As the hardware bridge linking AI Agents to the physical world and end users, intelligent hardware acts as a vital gateway for agents to perceive their environment and recognize user intent. Enabling AI Agents to maintain round‑the‑clock environmental awareness and efficiently capture real‑time user intentions is essential to improving their everyday service experience. This topic seeks to overcome the limitations of conventional visual perception systems. By deeply integrating sensing and computing, it explores full‑stack innovation spanning from low‑level hardware to high‑level algorithms. Key efforts include developing next‑generation sensors with real‑time understanding capabilities, investigating non‑traditional visual capture and compression techniques, and designing novel hardware architectures to run advanced algorithms—enabling highly efficient coordination across sensing, processing, and communication.

Topic Challenge: Break free from the framework of conventional sensing systems, explore novel sensors, signal processing and compression schemes to achieve highly energy-efficient sensing tasks, while enabling seamless integration with large models.

Topic Value: Breakthroughs in this research direction will enable intelligent hardware to better connect AI, users, and daily life. Against the backdrop of the AI Agent era, this will unlock the gateway to the next generation of intelligent hardware terminals and open up broader technological possibilities.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Launch & Scale Team

The Launch & Scale team builds the operating system that brings new sites, metros, and partners online and helps the network scale reliably. We turn complex dependencies into clear launch plans, readiness mechanisms, tools, and operating rhythms. We partner across infrastructure, permitting, flight operations, maintenance, commercial, partner readiness, and field operations. Our work stays close to real launches so that field lessons become repeatable systems rather than one-off fixes. As an intern, you will report to the Director, Launch & Site Operations and work closely with Launch Managers and cross-functional teams that bring the network online.

The Role

As the Launch & Scale Intern, you will contribute to a high-impact project that improves how Zipline plans, executes, and learns from launches. You will support Launch Managers by bringing structure to dependencies, analyzing readiness and performance, and helping teams turn field lessons into repeatable tools. You may spend time close to active launches, but you will work with experienced teammates rather than serve as the accountable launch owner. You will also own a clearly scoped project—such as a dashboard, process improvement, playbook, or lightweight automation—from problem definition through pilot and handoff. Along the way, you will receive coaching from the Director, Launch & Site Operations and collaborate with operators, engineers, commercial teammates, and field teams.

What You'll Do

- Support integrated launch plans for assigned workstreams by organizing milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, and open decisions.

- Analyze launch and site-operations data to identify bottlenecks, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve speed, quality, or repeatability.

- Prepare materials for readiness reviews and operating forums, including concise status summaries, action logs, and decision briefs.

- Work with Launch Managers and functional teams to follow up on commitments, reconcile conflicting information, and surface blockers early.

- Build or improve practical tools such as dashboards, playbooks, templates, checklists, or lightweight automations.

- Participate in selected onsite launch activities, capture field observations, and translate lessons into process improvements.

- Own a scoped internship project from problem definition through pilot, measurement, and an accepted handoff to the team.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in operations, engineering, business, supply chain, data and analytics, or a related field.

- Structured problem-solving skills and curiosity about how complex physical or technical systems work.

- Comfort with quantitative analysis, including spreadsheets and at least one data or automation tool such as SQL, Python, or a business-intelligence platform.

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex information easy to understand.

- Evidence of following through on a project involving multiple contributors through coursework, work, research, or extracurricular experience.

- Comfort operating in ambiguity, asking good questions, incorporating feedback, and staying reliable on details.

- Ability to work onsite in South San Francisco and willingness to travel occasionally within the United States to support launches.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

About us

The first baby boomers turn 80 this year. Over the next decade, the population most likely to need daily care will grow faster than the buildings, the staff, or the systems available to serve it.

Sage is the care intelligence platform for senior living and skilled nursing. We connect the hardware senior care runs on, including nurse call, fall management, and wander management, with software caregivers actually use. That consistent use is what produces reliable data, and reliable data is what gives operators a true picture of how their communities are running.

Sage is a collaborative team of ambitious, multi-disciplinary entrepreneurs on a mission to reinvent senior care with a modern operating system for caregivers. Millions of people depend on this care getting better, and we move with the urgency that deserves.

About this role

As a Software Engineering Intern at Sage, you'll join a product engineering team as a full member from day one. You'll attend the same standups, contribute to the same roadmap, review the same pull requests, and ship to the same production codebase as the rest of your team.

This internship runs Monday, June 7, 2027 to Friday, August 13, 2027.

The software you build supports caregivers responding to real residents in real moments of need. Every feature, bug fix, and improvement has the potential to make someone's day easier, and someone's care better.

Throughout the internship, you'll work closely with an experienced engineer who will mentor you, help you grow, and give you meaningful feedback. By the end of the summer, you'll have shipped production software and shared what you built with the broader engineering organization.

What you'll do

- Ship production code as part of a product engineering team, from your first pull request through deployment

- Build user-facing experiences in React and TypeScript used every day by caregivers and senior living communities

- Develop backend services in Java that power care workflows, notifications, and integrations with the systems our customers rely on

- Write tests, participate in code reviews, and iterate on feedback as part of our engineering process

- Partner with product managers, designers, and engineers to scope, build, and deliver meaningful features

- Learn what it takes to build and operate reliable software that people depend on every day

Minimum Qualifications

- Strong programming fundamentals in at least one language, such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, or Python, with excitement to learn across the stack

- Evidence that you enjoy building things, through coursework, personal projects, open source, internships, bootcamps, or self-directed work

- Familiarity with web fundamentals, including APIs, HTTP, and databases

- Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn quickly by asking thoughtful questions and acting on feedback

- Strong communication skills and enthusiasm for collaborating in an environment where ideas are shared and code is reviewed

- A genuine interest in building technology that serves people who are often overlooked by traditional software

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with React, Node.js, or a JVM language

- Exposure to SQL or other databases

- Experience using AI development tools such as Cursor, Claude, GitHub Copilot, or similar, along with the judgment to review and understand the code they generate

- A project you're excited to demo, regardless of its level of polish

- Interest in healthcare, aging, or mission-driven technology

What You'll Get

- Meaningful ownership of production software from day one

- A dedicated engineering mentor and regular, structured feedback

- A behind-the-scenes look at how a hardware-and-software company builds, ships, and supports products at scale

- The opportunity to present your work to the engineering organization and leave with real projects you can point to long after your internship ends

Compensation

Our headquarters are located near New York City's Union Square. We believe in cross team collaboration. We think good ideas can come from anyone, and we've designed our processes to encourage participation from all. While we take our mission seriously, we don't take ourselves too seriously. We like to host offsites, outings, and team meals where we can connect as people, not just as colleagues. We offer office lunch and a fully stocked snack bar. While we are an in-office culture, we allow up to 2 remote days per week.

This role is paid at $50/hour. As an internship position, it is not eligible for our standard employee benefits package (health insurance, stock options, PTO, etc.).

EEO Statement

Sage is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. Sage makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

About Wonder

Everything’s on the menu at Wonder. Except compromise.

Wonder is the mealtime platform built to feed every craving in one order. With Wonder, you can mix and match hundreds of dishes from 20+ exclusive restaurants in a single order, so everyone gets exactly what they’re craving. Enjoy everything from tacos to Thai with $0 delivery fees, plus dine-in or pick up at a Wonder location near you. Each dish is made to order on-site by our culinary team and served hot.

Behind the scenes, Wonder owns and operates every step of the dining experience, from recipe development to the technology that powers our experience, allowing us to deliver quality, variety, and consistency at scale.

Join us as we work to make great food more accessible.

About The Opportunity

The Growth Analytics team at Wonder serves as a strategic thought partner driving topline growth, customer acquisition, and customer lifetime value across our marketing and digital platforms. As a Growth Analytics Intern, you won't just pull numbers—you will dive into customer behavior, evaluate performance, and turn data into actionable business stories and strategic recommendations for the Growth Team. Working closely with full-time analytics leaders, you will leverage modern analytics tools (SQL, DBT, BigQuery, Looker) to help solve real-world growth hypotheses and directly influence strategic decisions in a fast-paced food-tech environment.

The Impact You Will Make

- Query BigQuery database environments using complex SQL, windows functions, CTEs, and different levels of aggregation to extract customer, order, and promotional performance data, moving from raw numbers to meaningful insights.

- Partner with growth and marketing stakeholders to evaluate campaign lift, customer cohort trends, and promotional A/B testing performance.

- Fully leverage Looker’s Gemini powered AI conversational analytics to draw insights from Looker explores and existing dashboards

- Manage and enhance the Growth Analytics AI data chatbot, ensuring alignment with AI governance frameworks and single-source-of-truth metric definitions.

- Translate complex data outputs into clear visual slides and executive summaries for quarterly cohort presentations and marketing strategy syncs.

Tangible Requirements and Essential Job Duties

- Formulate hypotheses and analyze ad-hoc growth questions (e.g., customer churn drivers, brand preferences, promo incrementality) to support key business choices.

- Validate data accuracy across marketing tracking channels and performance dashboards to ensure single-source-of-truth consistency.

- Synthesize findings into clear, structured takeaways and slide presentations that communicate strategic opportunities to non-technical stakeholders.

Initial Focus and Key Deliverables (Post-Joining)

- First 30 Days: Complete team onboarding, gain fluency in Wonder’s data stack (BigQuery, Looker, DBT), and build a solid understanding of core growth metrics.

- First 60 Days: Take ownership of recurring marketing performance analyses and co-author strategic deep dives on customer engagement or promotional performance under mentor guidance.

- First 90 Days: Own and execute an end-to-end strategic capstone project (i.e., investigating a high-value customer cohort or evaluating a growth campaign to re-engage customers) using artificial intelligence and present strategic recommendations to Growth leadership.

Core Responsibilities

- Act as an active strategic contributor by bringing curiosity, fresh perspectives, and structured problem-solving to growth challenges.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Marketing, CRM, and Operations teams to answer strategic questions with data-backed insights.

- Continuous learning: continuously refine your analytical toolset, business intuition, and data storytelling abilities.

What You Bring to the Table

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business Analytics, Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Business Administration, or a related quantitative field (Must Have).

- 0–1 years (Currently enrolled student; prior internship, research, or relevant project/coursework experience is a plus).

- Foundational SQL skills (SELECT statements, JOINs, GROUP BY, aggregations) and comfort working with relational databases.

- Business acumen and strong strategic curiosity with a desire to answer the "why" behind customer behaviors and business trends.

- Familiarity with data visualization tools (Looker, Tableau, Power BI) or advanced Google Sheets/Excel skills for data modeling and charts.

- Strong data storytelling skills with the ability to summarize technical data into concise, strategic bullet points and slides.

- Exposure to or strong interest in digital marketing, e-commerce, customer retention/cohort analysis, and promotional strategy.

- Collaborative attitude, detail orientation, and proactive communication skills in a fast-moving startup environment.

As a matter of company policy, Wonder does not sponsor applicants for employment visa status for this role.

Our hybrid model requires 3 days a week in the office. That said, many team members choose to come in more often to take advantage of in-person collaboration and connection. You're welcome—and encouraged—to be in the office up to 5 days a week if it works for you.

At Wonder, we build the best teams by hiring with an objective lens — evaluating people for their potential while championing diversity, equity, and inclusion. Our vision is to build a global edge traffic infrastructure platform and become the long-term cornerstone of ByteDance's global edge business in terms of scale, performance, and cost.

We are looking for talented individuals to join us for an internship. Our internship program offers students hands-on experience, industry exposure, and opportunities to apply their knowledge to real-world challenges while building a strong foundation for personal and professional growth.
Interns will gain practical experience, explore potential career paths, and participate in social events, learning programs, and development workshops alongside industry professionals.

- Currently pursuing an Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
- Solid foundation in software engineering fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer networks).
- Programming experience in one or more languages such as Go, C or Rust, demonstrated through coursework, personal projects, or open-source contributions.
- Familiarity with Linux and basic understanding of containers, distributed systems, or networking concepts.
- Strong problem-solving skills, a growth mindset, ownership, and eagerness to learn in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Prior internship, co-op, or research experience related to backend/systems development, cloud-native technologies, or infrastructure.
- Hands-on exposure to containers and Kubernetes through coursework, side projects, or internships (e.g., deploying applications, basic cluster operations, service discovery, Ingress/Gateway).
- Contributions to cloud-native open-source projects (e.g., Kubernetes, Containerd, Cilium/eBPF), even at a small scale.
- Deeper Linux knowledge (kernel, scheduling, TCP/IP, routing, iptables/nftables) gained through projects or self-study.

About the role

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for an internship position to help develop and test our wireless sensing hardware. The successful candidate will work closely with our team of engineers and researchers to design, simulate, analyze, tape out, integrate, and validate advanced antenna systems. This role offers hands-on experience across full product lifecycle, with a focus on design optimization and performance reliability. This internship offers a chance to work on hard problems of great impact and a unique opportunity for direct involvement in 0-to-1 product development within a dynamic and collaborative startup environment.

What you'll do

- Design and evaluation of antennas for a given wireless channel link budget starting from first-principles, while considering pros/cons of different solutions and trade-off between KPIs

- Perform computational electromagnetic simulations and develop new simulation models using full-wave EM software tools

- Analyze and interpret simulation results, providing insights and recommendations for design improvements and performance optimization

- Build mock ups for proof-of-concept prototypes and test vehicles, build test fixtures and platforms, and create solutions to automate the antenna system development process, and data analysis of testing workflows

- Assist in PCB layout design process, and DFM reviews -considering mass production readiness- with vendors and external manufacturing partners

- Integrate antennas into complete device form factor by collaborating with cross-functional teams

- Carry out antenna characterization and ensure that the antennas integrated in our products meet their specifications in free space and on-body from prototype to mass production

- Assist in sensor calibration to reduce device-to-device variability and maintain reliable performance in different operating conditions and practical user-study cases across user populations

- Optimize hardware system for low-noise/low-interference, high-resolution signal detection and processing, and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and power budget

- Document designs, experiments, and studies; and clearly report findings and recommendations to the wider team

- Hands-on experience in microwave measurement equipment (vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, etc.)

- Hands-on experience designing, prototyping and building functional antenna systems

- High work ethic, enthusiasm, flexibility, and resourcefulness

- Excellent problem-solving skills, and ability to work independently and take initiative

- Strong communication and documentation skills, and ability to work well in a team and across disciplines

- Experience in on-body or implantable wireless devices, sensing, imaging applications

- Experience in any of: UWB, directional miniaturized antennas, multiband antennas, flexible electronics, e-textiles, ultra-low power wireless systems, integrated sensing and comms

- Experience in design optimization and inverse design techniques for electromagnetics structures • Experience in de-sense, coexistence, EMC/EMI and OTA performance

We are an early-stage AI startup building the first AI-native productivity assistant that seamlessly integrates into your digital life to handle email, calendars, contacts, and tasks and make sure you never drop the ball. Backed by leading venture capital firms including Village Global, Neo, SV Angel, and researchers and executives from Anthropic, Microsoft, Cognition, Quora, Atlassian, and Waymo, we’re assembling a world-class founding team passionate about building scalable, human-aligned AI systems that transform how life gets done.

Our founding team includes repeat entrepreneurs, AI researchers, and early engineers from companies such as Meta, Palantir, Dropbox, and Databricks. Collectively, we’ve built products used by millions, led teams at unicorn-stage AI companies, raised over $100 million in venture capital, and achieved exits to Fortune 500 firms. Together, we bring deep expertise across AI systems design, large-scale engineering, and growth at the intersection of technology and human productivity.

The Role

As a Software Engineering Intern, you’ll work closely with our founding team to help design, prototype, and scale components of our agentic AI assistant.

This is a hands-on opportunity to do work at the intersection of systems design thinking with AI engineering fundamentals, contributing directly to the architecture and functionality of real, production-bound technology.

You’ll have mentorship from experienced engineers and founders building next-generation AI systems and gain valuable exposure to startup operations, while maintaining meaningful ownership over your projects and deliverables.

What You’ll Do

- Collaborate with engineers to design and implement core infrastructure and backend components.

- Develop core features across the AI stack — including orchestration logic, API integrations, and LLM-based workflows.

- Build diagnostic tools, write test cases, and implement monitoring systems for reliability and consistency.

- Contribute to the design and improvement of our agent reasoning and execution pipelines.

- Participate in product and architecture discussions with the founding team.

- Document bugs, issues, and edge cases; help refine and stabilize our platform for launch-readiness.

Who You Are

- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, AI, or related field (or equivalent experience).

- Strong foundation in software engineering and systems design thinking — you enjoy reasoning about architecture, scalability, and tradeoffs.

- Experience with Python, JavaScript, or Go; familiarity with AI frameworks (e.g. LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar) is a plus.

- Interest or prior experience in agent development, LLM APIs, or applied AI engineering.

- Excited by early-stage environments and fast-paced, iterative work.

- Available full-time for one academic quarter or semester in Winter/Spring/Summer 2026.

Nice to Have

- Experience building prototypes or projects that integrate AI models or autonomous agents.

- Exposure to distributed systems, vector databases, or API orchestration.

- Previous internship or research experience in applied AI or software engineering.

- Contributions to open-source or personal AI/automation projects.

What You’ll Gain

- Direct mentorship from experienced AI and systems engineers.

- Opportunity to work on cutting-edge agentic AI technology in a startup environment.

- End-to-end ownership of meaningful projects that may evolve into core product features.

- Exposure to startup operations, product iteration, and the engineering culture of an early-stage team.

New Graduate Engineer, Manufacturing (Starshield)

Hawthorne, CA

Apply

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER. MANUFACTURING (STARSHIELD)

As an engineer within the Starshield Manufacturing organization, you will have the exciting opportunity to utilize your knowledge, experience, and creativity to develop novel solutions at the cutting edge of space technology. Expect to learn new skills, to work hands on with hardware, and to solve engineering problems across manufacturing and production domains. You will provide input into the development and optimization of our new and existing products. You will also collaborate cross functionally and be a vital part of the relationship between our engineering and production teams.

The manufacturing team has a variety of disciplines and skillsets vital to the successful build, test, and utilization of Starshield products. An engineer on this team must have a working knowledge of design, schematics, operations, manufacturing, testing, and flight. They should also demonstrate sound engineering intuition and critical thinking and be comfortable working under ambiguous requirements with minimal oversight. Combining these skills, these engineers face challenges across a wide variety of work centers at the company, and the team is frequently asked to tackle new, inter-departmental development projects. The ultimate goal of the Manufacturing team is to ensure that satellites and customers achieve their mission.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team (design, build, and reliability engineers) and operations to efficiently build parts on schedule.

- Develop and revise production processes, procedures, equipment, tooling, and layout.

- Drive design for manufacturing and assembly during new product development and improvement cycles.

- Facilitate production of flight-qualified hardware at increasing production rate while reducing cost.

- Resolve complex manufacturing defects and eliminate root cause.

- Support design for manufacturing and assembly during new product development and improvement cycles.

- Manage integration build flow and test operations.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, computer engineering or other engineering discipline

- Graduating with a bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or PhD in 2026 or 2027

- Experience in design or manufacturing engineering (internships, extracurricular and academic projects apply)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Master's degree in an engineering discipline

- Demonstrated experience working in a highly adaptive and iterative environment.

- Proven excellence in a high volume commercial, aerospace, or automotive manufacturing environment.

- Experience transitioning products from design to manufacturing and scaling to high volume as part of a cross-functional team.

- Experience with DOE, gage R&R and process qualifications.

- Experience defining production data requirements and SPC.

- Ability to design tooling for high volume manufacturing.

- Demonstrated experience implementing automation into production processes.

- Experience integrating electromechanical or lamination assemblies with both manual and automated processes.

- Ability to develop and maintain high performing suppliers and contract manufacturers.

- Experience with NX and Teamcenter.

- Experience working with and defining requirements for ERP, MRP and MES systems.

- Ability and willingness to obtain a Top Secret clearance

- Experience with MATLAB, Python, or other programming language

- Demonstrated engineering intuition, critical thinking, comfort with ambiguity

ADDITIONAL SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Some travel to other SpaceX sites may be required as needed, up to 10%

- Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet mission-critical deadlines

- This position is very hands-on and requires one to be on their feet for extended periods of time, up to 4 hours at a time

- Will often work side by side with our technicians and must be able to climb ladders, stoop, bend, crawl, and work in tight spaces

- An active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions; if so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $100,000.00 - $130,000.00
Level 2: $115,000.00 - $160,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

- To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
